missionPremise: Today a caller can look up A PARCEL and cannot ask a question ACROSS parcels. P-106 adds the second thing as a PROJECTION over facets that are already baked, not a pipeline, and the design idea it exists to get right is that a filter over a rail with gaps returns THREE SETS - matched, excluded, and not-evaluated with the rail named - because including the unmeasured fabricates a claim and excluding them silently hides parcels that might qualify. Source: _inbox/2026-09-01_p106_constraint_search_WDLL.md, operator go 2026-09-01, OPS-16 amendment A-071.
completionPredicate: A land buyer can express a constraint over one Central Texas county and get back three sets from a cache that declares when it was built, with every refusal declared rather than errored, and can push the matched ids onto a screen with no re-fetch; every check shown failing on a deliberate violation and passing on restore.
scopeBasis: Serve path only, in legacy-design-tools. No acquisition path, no facet re-derivation, no second store for a subject that already has one, no ranking, no owner data, no tier-gate changes. Six Central Texas counties, because landing_parcel_jurisdiction covers 981,405 of roughly 7.6M Texas parcels and a statewide answer would imply coverage that does not exist. DDL written and HANDED BACK UNAPPLIED per the dispatch.

acceptanceItems.title: The projection table
whatPassed: One row per parcel per county, a column pair (value + NOT NULL state) per rail, builtAt and bakeSnapshotAt on every row, and a build ledger that a build cannot skip.

Built from the baked facets: every cell's `basis` names the bake field, the landing row, or the atom it came from. No facet is re-derived and no second store is created for a subject that already has one.
The migration applied cleanly to a throwaway database, all 31 constraints enumerated from pg_catalog, 8 deliberate violations refused, 3 corrected rows accepted, exactly 3 rows admitted.
The migration's constraints and the drizzle schema's constraints were diffed: byte-identical, 31 rows each, and the diff was shown able to fire.

The derivation was run over ten LIVE Bastrop parcels and compared to the LIVE get_smart_site: flood agrees 10 of 10, landUse agrees 10 of 10, zoning agrees on all 5 parcels where the bake carries a district.
whyPartial: The projection table is NOT BUILT. The migration is handed back unapplied by instruction, so no row exists, `builtAt` has never been written, and the row-count reconciliation against the bake could only be run as the SELECT half. That is stated rather than narrated as done.

The 'a parcel's projected value matches get_smart_site' check FAILS on zoning for unincorporated parcels: the projection says `absent-verified`, the serve path says `unknown`, on 50,157 of 77,799 Bastrop parcels and 346,165 across the six counties. The cause is that the projection uses two independently derived inputs and get_smart_site uses one. Routed to the operator below; pinned by a named test so it cannot drift.

whatContradictedTheCard.summary: The card's proposed v1 rail list is wrong on four rails. The measurement wins, per item 1.
whatContradictedTheCard.marketValue_landValue_improvementValue_y: ZERO present in the tier-1 bake in ALL SIX counties. Not low - zero. cad_property carries the values at source; the bake's cadRoll block does not, because node-facet-patch-cad-roll has not run for these counties. Reading cad_property directly would be re-deriving from source, which item 2 forbids. whatContradictedTheCard.etj: NO SOURCE EXISTS in the deployment store. tx_city_boundary, tx_county_boundary, tx_special_district and landing_parcel_jurisdiction are what is there; nothing carries an extraterritorial ring, and landing_parcel_jurisdiction.disposition is CHECK-constrained to in-city | unincorporated | unresolved. Carried as a declared-ahead column per the rails-v2 ruling, `unread` on every row.
whatContradictedTheCard.landUse: 0.0% in Caldwell and Travis, 0.03% in McLennan, 20.2% Bastrop, 75.5% Hays, 84.9% Williamson. Searchable per county, never per program.
whatContradictedTheCard.zoningDistrict: The card treats it as one rail. Its PRESENT count is 12.3% to 46.6%, but its EVALUABLE share once the two-input absent-verified rule is applied is 42.8% to 76.8%. The absent-verified half is two to five times the present half and is the half that answers 'unzoned land'.
whatContradictedTheCard.whatTheCardGotRight: The situs sentinel. The card predicted roughly 21 points of Bastrop overstatement from a naive non-null test; measured 20.7 (74,820 naive vs 58,716 real of 77,799). The measurement adds that this is Bastrop-specific: Travis and Williamson are at 0.0 points, so a fleet-wide rule derived from Bastrop would be over-fitted.
whatContradictedTheCard.reltuplesConfirmed: All five of the card's magnitude figures re-measured today and identical.

operatorRulingsRequested.question: The unmeasured share above which a filter on a rail is REFUSED for that county.
operatorRulingsRequested.whyItIsYours: The card states it explicitly: propose a number with the evidence, do not pick one silently and do not ship a default. Nothing in the code defaults it; unset means no gate, and coverage is reported on every success regardless.
operatorRulingsRequested.reasoningInOneLine: A search must be able to evaluate a MAJORITY of the county it claims to search. That is a principle rather than a fit to today's numbers, and it fires today rather than being dormant.

evidence.unmeasuredSharesAreBimodal: Every rail that works anywhere is between 0.0% and 57.2% unmeasured; every rail that does not work is at exactly 100.0%. Nothing sits between 58% and 99%, so any ceiling in that whole range refuses the same set and would fire only on rails that are already obviously dead.
evidence.at40pct: refuses 13 of 36 live rail-county pairs, including every rail Caldwell has. A control whose scope is broader than its claim is a defect too.
evidence.at50pct: refuses 8 of 36: Williamson flood (53.0%), cityLimits (53.1%) and specialDistrict (53.1%); Caldwell zoning (57.2%); landUse in Bastrop, Caldwell, McLennan and Travis. EVERY county keeps at least three searchable rails - Bastrop 5, Caldwell 4, Hays 6, McLennan 5, Travis 5, Williamson 3. That was measured, not assumed.
evidence.at60pctOr70pct: identical to each other: refuses landUse in four counties and nothing else, and ADMITS Williamson flood at 53.0% unmeasured - a search that cannot look at half the county presenting itself as a search, which is the exact thing item 5 exists to prevent.

operatorRulingsRequested.howToApply: Set CONSTRAINT_SEARCH_UNMEASURED_REFUSE_ABOVE_PCT=50 on the api-server service. Unset, nothing refuses on this ground and unmeasuredPctByRail still ships on every response.
operatorRulingsRequested.reversalCriterion: If the cadRoll patch and further flood writes move several rails into the 50-60 band, the bimodality that makes 50 cheap disappears and the number should be re-derived from a fresh census rather than nudged.

operatorRulingsRequested.question: The zoning divergence: does get_smart_site adopt the two-input derivation, or does the projection drop to `unknown`?
operatorRulingsRequested.whyItIsYours: It changes what a customer sees on 346,165 parcels, and both answers are defensible.
operatorRulingsRequested.optionA: Teach composeSmartSiteStub the same two-input rule. get_smart_site starts reporting zoning `absent-verified` instead of `unknown` on unincorporated parcels with no district, which is a strictly better answer and the one a land buyer actually wants. Cost: it changes a live customer-visible rail on 346,165 parcels and needs its own card, because the stub currently takes no jurisdiction input at all.
operatorRulingsRequested.optionB: Drop the projection to `unknown` on zoning so the two agree. Cost: the `absent` operator loses its most useful rail, 'unzoned land' becomes unanswerable, and zoning's searchable share falls from 42.8-76.8% back to 12.3-46.6%.
operatorRulingsRequested.laneRecommendation: Option A, as its own card. The projection is already the better-informed of the two and the divergence is not a defect in it; the cheaper fix would throw away the capability the card was written to create.
operatorRulingsRequested.pinnedBy: artifacts/api-server/src/lib/parcelConstraintProjection.test.ts, test `PINNED DIVERGENCE: the projection earns absent-verified on zoning where get_smart_site says unknown`. It asserts the two DISAGREE, so if either side changes the test fails and the change has to be deliberate.

countsWithTheirCountingRules.railCensusDenominator: tier-1 bake rows per county: one row per place_key matching node:<fips>:% under adapter_key='node-facets:tier1'. NOT the CAD row count, NOT the TxGIO parcel count, NOT the landing-table row count; those three differ from it and from each other.
countsWithTheirCountingRules.byRail: notEvaluated.byRail[r] counts PARCELS in the not-evaluated set whose rail r could not be evaluated. A parcel missing two rails increments both, so byRail values SUM TO MORE than the set count and are not a partition. Same rule for excluded.byRail. The set counts are the partition.
countsWithTheirCountingRules.unmeasuredPctByRail: the rail's unevaluable share of the WHOLE county, not of the not-evaluated set, computed in the same statement as the answer so the refusal's number and the result's number come from one snapshot.
countsWithTheirCountingRules.magnitudes: pg_class.reltuples, ESTIMATES, stated as such because a full count(*) on these tables times out under writer load.
countsWithTheirCountingRules.zoningEvaluable: (present + absent-verified) / bake parcels, where absent-verified requires BOTH no district in the bake AND landing_parcel_jurisdiction saying unincorporated.

LESSON: A pg_dump-generated test fixture can be refreshed surgically without regenerating the whole thing WRONG: dump the pushed schema with the repo's own pipeline, diff against the committed fixture, and confirm ZERO removed lines before writing. Here the regenerated file was a strict superset (+114, -0), which proves the local pg_dump formats identically to whatever produced the committed one. pg_dump 18 adds \restrict / \unrestrict lines that the repo's grep filter does not strip; they must be removed by hand or CI sees drift.

In Git Bash, `grep -vE '^\\restrict '` does NOT match a line starting with a backslash, and neither does the same pattern in a Python heredoc where bash mangles the escapes. `awk 'substr($0,1,1) != "\\"'` does. A filter that silently matches nothing looks exactly like a filter that had nothing to match.

`cmd | grep -v ...; echo $?` reports the GREP's exit code, so a typecheck that failed printed 'ok'. DEV_PROCESS 2.3 exactly, and it caught a real TS2322 in a test file that a piped check had reported clean. Redirect to a file and read $? directly.

Adding one MCP tool breaks six hardcoded counts across five test files plus one in a source string. The source string was changed to derive from the catalog (`SMARTSITE_MCP_TOOLS.length`) so the next tool cannot desynchronise it; the test assertions are deliberately left literal, because a test that re-derives the number it is checking cannot fail.

The api-server suite's per-file `createTestSchema` beforeAll times out at 30s under CPU contention, producing 37 file-level failures that look like real breakage and are not. Run it alone. Two full suite runs plus a tsc --build concurrently is enough to trigger it.

The refreshed schema fixture carries the 0094 CHECK constraints INLINE in the CREATE TABLE, so `withTestSchema` replays them into every per-file test schema. The value/state invariant is therefore armed in CI today, before the migration is ever applied to production - which is the only place it is armed until then.

A full 3,447-test suite on this machine fails at the FILE level with `Hook timed out in 30000ms` in per-file schema creation, in 3 of 4 attempts, including on a fresh database with nothing else running. It looks exactly like real breakage. The discriminator is to TIME THE THING BLAMED: the DDL replay was 2,616 ms on the new fixture and 2,895 ms on the old one, so the fixture was exonerated by measurement rather than by argument. A bounded, repeatable subset comparison is worth more than an unrepeatable full run.
